title: Microsoft Purview: archive SharePoint files with retention policies
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, opt-in default, licensing, storage billing and configuration instructions are supported by the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. A minor checklist/table mismatch remains for archive-storage monitoring.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No API or PowerShell call is documented for configuring a retention policy's archive action.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention archive action PowerShell New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-RetentionComplianceRule archive parameter; Microsoft 365 Archive retention archive action Microsoft Graph API retention label archive settings. Read both rule references and retention-settings.

claims.claim: The Archive billing-policy connection is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Microsoft 365 Archive > Connect a policy.
claims.quote:
go to **Billing > Pay-as-you-go**.
Select **Connect your services**, or go to the **Services** tab and find **Microsoft 365 Archive**. Select **Connect a policy**

claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented for connecting Archive to its pay-as-you-go billing policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive billing policy connection automation PowerShell API connect service billing; "Microsoft 365 Archive" "PowerShell" "billing policy". Read archive-setup and billing-node guidance; results for Backup and High Volume Email do not establish Archive automation.

claims.claim: Earlier tenants can use Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services.
claims.quote: For tenants that use **Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services** to turn on Archive, turn it off in the same location:

claims.claim: No admin UI setting is documented for hiding the manual Archive action while retaining policy archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive hide manual Archive action admin center UI AllowFileArchive. Read archive-manage, archive-faq and retention-settings; they direct administrators to PowerShell rather than an admin UI setting.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchive $false hides the manual Archive action tenant-wide without blocking policy archiving.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchive $false
This tenant setting overrides the site-level property with the same name and blocks manual file archiving across the tenant. Admin-defined policies can still archive eligible files automatically.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator can configure manual file archiving.
claims.quote: [SharePoint Administrators] or [Global Administrators] can control manual file archiving for all SharePoint sites, a subset of sites, or not at all.

claims.claim: Get-SPOSite reports site archive-file storage through ArchivedFileDiskUsed.
claims.quote: The '*ArchivedFileDiskUsed*' property of the ***Get-SPOSite*** cmdlet indicates the storage consumed by all archived files on that site in bytes.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site_url> -AllowFileArchive $false hides the manual Archive action on the specified site.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site_url> -AllowFileArchive $false

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault $false disables manual archiving by default on sites created later.
claims.quote: To control whether users can manually archive files on sites created in the future, use the ***-AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault*** property of the ***Set-SPOTenant*** cmdlet.

claims.claim: For a retention policy or label to archive files, its retention settings must include the archive action rather than merely enabling manual archiving.
claims.quote: Existing retention policies and labels don't archive files unless an administrator updates them to include the archive action.

claims.claim: The New-RetentionComplianceRule reference lists no archive parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention archive action PowerShell New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-RetentionComplianceRule archive parameter. Read the complete New-RetentionComplianceRule reference; no archive parameter and RetentionComplianceAction values are Delete, Keep and KeepAndDelete.

claims.claim: The Set-RetentionComplianceRule reference lists no archive parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention archive action PowerShell New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-RetentionComplianceRule archive parameter. Read the complete Set-RetentionComplianceRule reference; no archive parameter and RetentionComplianceAction values are Delete, Keep and KeepAndDelete.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects the documented E5 requirement plus Archive pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: File-level archive requires a [Microsoft 365 E5 license]. No additional setup is required to archive files by using retention policies or labels. To use the cost-saving benefits of Microsoft 365 Archive, first [set up pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 Archive].

claims.claim: The variable cost rating corresponds to a metered Archive storage charge.
claims.quote: Storage consumption is charged at a per-GB monthly rate.

claims.claim: Archived files need reactivation before they can be read.
claims.quote: After a file is archived, it requires reactivation before it can be read.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The archive-storage monitoring check in the governance checklist has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Review archive storage against the tenant quota and the pay-as-you-go bill; Get-SPOSite reports ArchivedFileDiskUsed per site." Table rows cover retention archiving, billing connection and the manual Archive action, not storage monitoring.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet beginning 'Review archive storage against the tenant quota' because its monitoring control has no corresponding table row.
